Subject: Re: Overiding master.cf problems

Gary W. Smith wrote:
> Hello, 
>
> I have 4 postfix in dev that do a lot of different things.  I got a new server and would like to put all of these instances on a single postfix instance.  Because each instance has different settings (because they do different things) I figured the best approach would be to use a default main.cf file and just override the settings with the master.cf
>
> This worked fine for all of the instances but one, in which I had a custom smtpd_recipient_restrction that uses sqlgrey, which seems to fail because there is a space in the line...
>
> WORKS:
> 10.80.65.2:smtp       inet  n       -       n       -       -       smtpd 
>  -o content_filter=scan:[10.80.66.2]:3654
>  -o smtpd_recipient_restrictions=permit_mynetworks,reject_unknown_sender_domain,reject_unauth_pipelining,reject_unauth_destination,reject_invalid_hostname
>  -o relay_recipient_maps=mysql:/etc/postfix/mysql/relay-recipients.mysql
>  -o relay_transport=mysql:/etc/postfix/mysql/relay-transport.mysql
>  -o relay_domains=mysql:/etc/postfix/mysql/relay-domains.mysql
>  -o transport_maps=mysql:/etc/postfix/mysql/transport.mysql
>  
> FAILS: (note that this one has check_policy_service inet: in it).  It seems to die on the space
> 10.80.65.2:smtp  inet  n       -       n       -       -       smtpd 
>  -o content_filter=scan:[10.80.66.2]:3654
>  -o smtpd_recipient_restrictions=permit_mynetworks,reject_unknown_sender_domain,check_policy_service inet:10.80.66.250:5847,reject_unauth_pipelining,reject_unauth_destination,reject_invalid_hostname
>  -o relay_recipient_maps=mysql:/etc/postfix/mysql/relay-recipients.mysql
>  -o relay_transport=mysql:/etc/postfix/mysql/relay-transport.mysql
>  -o relay_domains=mysql:/etc/postfix/mysql/relay-domains.mysql
>  -o transport_maps=mysql:/etc/postfix/mysql/transport.mysql
>
> Is there a way to do this in the master.cf?  
>   


define variables in main.cf and use them in master.cf. As a side 
benefit, this will avoid too much clutter in master.cf, and you can put 
comments to document each parameter...

== master.cf:

smtpd ...
    ...
    - o smtpd_recipient_restrictions=$instance4_recipient_restrictions
    ...

== main.cf:
instance4_recipient_restrictions =
    #first we do_me_do
    do_me_do
    # then we do you do
    do_you_do
    # and we ...
    bada_boom
